messages:
oncall-bot: Incident created: 3890012345 - Multiple 5xx/503s observed for hosted inference. Auto-triage flagged upstream worker exits.

kevin_s: seeing a sudden spike in 503s starting ~10:11 UTC. Started around a model swap.

maria_r: customer (Acme Corp) opened support ticket — many requests timing out, 5xx from gateway. Sending diag link.

support_anna: escalated to oncall at 10:15. Customer is on Dedicated plan, high priority. They reported latency + "server error" on many requests.

infra_sre: checked node logs — worker PID 4321 segfaulted repeatedly. Container restarted by k8s. NVML reports OOM around same time on GPU0.

eng-runtime: grabbed coredump, looks like crash in attention kernel during kv-cache resize after model swap. Suspect race between prefetch and model variant reload.

kevin_s: dropping relevant log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T10:11:58Z] INFO prefetch: started background prefetch batch_id=987
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] ERROR worker[4321]: GPU allocation failed: out of memory allocating 1.2GiB
[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] FATAL worker[4321]: SIGSEGV at 0x7f9e6c2a4b3c (in attn_kernel)
[2026-03-17T10:12:04Z] kubelet: container exit code 139, restarted
```

maria_r: repro seems to require: model swap+prefetch enabled+burst qps (~350 rps) + long seq (>=4096). Happened when batch map scaled up to 32.

eng-runtime: quick triage suggests race when kv-cache resize interleaves with prefetch GPU allocations. Prefetch may allocate large scratch buffers assuming the old model config. On model swap the required buffer size increases and triggers OOM while kernel still running -> segfault.

tanaka: starting a controlled rollback to previous model variant (v2.1) in the affected cluster, will canary 10% then 50%->100%.

infra_sre: created ticket INF-8274 and attached coredump + nvml logs. Pinning affected node to maintenance to avoid noisy restarts.

kevin_s: immediate mitigation options: disable background prefetch globally for hosted region, throttle batchmap max_batch_size to 16, and add a firewall rule to route heavy tenants to fallback model. Which is fastest?

eng-runtime: fastest is disable prefetch via feature flag (deploy in 5m). Throttle batchmap needs a rolling restart on runner which is slower. We'll push the prefetch toggle.

support_anna: notifying customer: "We're investigating. Short-term mitigation in progress, will update in 30 minutes."

oncall-bot: Action: featureflag prefetch=false targeting region-us-east scheduled at 10:30 UTC.

kevin_s: prefetch toggle applied at 10:31 — monitoring. Error rate down from 6% -> 0.8% over 10m.

maria_r: customer confirms fewer errors and some slow responses but no 5xx. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime: follow-up plan: reproduce locally with model-swap + concurrent prefetch, add boundary checks on kv resize, and add a pre-swap drain step to stop prefetch/allocations during model replacement. Also add an alert for sudden allocation spikes.

tanaka: opening PR to add model-swap drain hook: GH#4021. Another PR with allocation guard in kernel pending GH#4022. Will run perf tests.

infra_sre: keeping node in maintenance until new build validated. Scheduling canary deploy to staging then prod.

kevin_s: tagging for postmortem. Please include: repro steps, exact model configs (seq length/batch), prefetch behavior, and customer impact timeline.

support_anna: customer updated at 11:05 that errors subsided after mitigation, asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

eng-runtime: ETA for fix (drain+guard) is 3 business days if PRs pass tests; can expedite if needed.

maria_r: adding metrics note: kv_prefetch_alloc_bytes spiked to 4.3GiB before OOM. Will add a dashboard widget.

oncall-bot: Incident assigned: eng-runtime. Priority: P1.

kevin_s: great job all. We'll follow-up with a blameless postmortem and link to INF-8274 and GH#4021/4022.

support_anna: I'll keep customer informed and close the support escalation once fix is deployed.

eng-runtime: leaving a TODO: run long-run soak testing with model swaps under synthetic load to catch regressions.

maria_r: closing on-call handoff, thanks everyone.
